features: New — Direct settlement entry. A new item under Movements lets you record, in a few seconds, the expenses that arise and are settled at the same moment: stamp duty, bank charges, direct debits, small expenses. Just enter amount, description, expense account and cash account: the system creates a single accounting entry (cost against bank) without opening any supplier ledger. Until now, recording a bank charge meant inventing a "Bank" supplier, issuing an invoice, paying it and — if anything went wrong — producing a credit note: six documents for two euros fifty. The expense account stays linked, so budget and allocation work exactly as they do for an invoice. The form can be filled entirely from the keyboard (Tab to move between fields, Enter to save, Esc to leave) and shows a live preview of the double-entry record. If you pick a supplier subject to withholding tax the system warns you before saving and points you to the invoice flow, because in that case the amount must be split between the net due to the supplier and the tax due to the Revenue Agency. Every entry can be reversed, which creates the mirror record while leaving the original untouched.

Important — A financial year containing accounting entries can no longer be deleted. Until now a closed year could be removed, and with it all its journal entries, detail lines and links to instalments disappeared in cascade, with no warning. What remained were instalment shares with amounts marked as paid and no movement to justify them. Deletion is now allowed only on years that never had any movement.

Important — A building can have only one open financial year at a time. With two years open at once the system could not determine where to record current movements, and the choice could change from one operation to the next. Creating or reopening a second year is now rejected with an explicit message. The rule also applies to the year created automatically when a new building is added. If your archive already contains two open years (for example after restoring a backup taken before this version) you can still edit and rename them: the block only applies when opening a new one.

Important — An invoice with payments already recorded can no longer be reversed directly. Previously the reversal created the credit note even when the invoice had been paid: this left a cash outflow with no debt to justify it and, if the credit note was later deleted, an invoice showing as "open" while payments were still active. The system now asks you to reverse the payments first, then the invoice. In addition, when the credit note of a reversal is deleted, the original invoice status is no longer forced to "open" but recalculated from the payments actually present.

Important — Credit notes generated automatically by a reversal no longer appear among the credits available for offsetting. They are not documents issued by the supplier: they exist only to cancel out the invoice they reverse. Using one to settle another invoice would have recorded the extinction of a debt towards a supplier who still considers that document unpaid, without a single euro leaving the account. Credit notes genuinely received from the supplier remain available for offsetting as before.

Accounting fix — Collections using available credit. When a collection combined cash and existing credit and the total exceeded the instalment due, the surplus was recorded on the cash entry even though it was funded by the credit: the journal came out unbalanced by that amount, silently. The surplus is now attributed to the correct entry, and credit drawn but not used is returned to the resident, who only consumes the portion actually needed to cover the debt.

Fix — The payment date cannot be later than today, because it describes a movement that has already taken place and is used as the journal recording date. The check now accounts for the Italian time zone, so those working late at night are no longer refused the current date. Payments already in the archive with a future date remain editable.

Fix — When editing an invoice, the budget capacity check no longer counts the invoice itself among the amounts already committed. Previously the amount was counted twice and the system reported a non-existent overrun, asking for a justification that was then discarded on save.

Fix — Issuing an instalment made up entirely of zero or negative shares no longer generates an empty accounting entry. Those records stayed in the journal with no lines and piled up with every new issue.

Security — Strengthened the building-ownership check on every value entered in movements: expense account, property unit, bank account, invoices to pay, cash accounts, management sets, instalment shares, contacts and parent account in the chart of accounts. Nothing changes in normal use; the protection prevents data belonging to another building from being attached by mistake to an accounting entry.

Accounting checks extended to collections, collection reversals and instalment issues: every entry generated by these operations is now verified in double entry before being saved, as was already the case for invoices and payments.

Chart of accounts: a sub-account left at zero is no longer offered as a "parent chapter" when creating or editing an expense item, and an item can no longer be set as its own child. Previously the parent list was based only on the amount being zero, so an empty sub-account was mistaken for a chapter; the item being edited also appeared among its own possible parents. The list now offers only top-level items, excluding the item being edited and its sub-accounts.
This update does not change the database structure: no migration to run.
